claims.text: A strong low-field magnetocaloric response in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys is driven by magnetostructural coupling mediated by nanoscale lattice heterogeneities.
Intrinsic compositional disorder creates localized lattice distortions.
Localized lattice distortions enhance changes in magnetic-moment alignment under small applied fields.
Enhanced field-induced magnetic-moment alignment changes produce a significant magnetic entropy change.
The proposed distortion-mediated response yields low magnetic hysteresis.
The proposed distortion-mediated response permits rapid heat exchange.
An overall uniform structural network maintains mechanical stability despite local heterogeneity.
The as-cast alloy contains inherent nanoscale chemical and lattice heterogeneities.
Controlled thermal annealing can reduce local lattice distortions and chemical heterogeneities.
Chemical disorder strengthens coupling between the lattice and magnetic moments through localized lattice distortions.
Magnetostructural coupling facilitates magnetic-moment reorientation and a large entropy change at fields below approximately 1 T.
The distributed nature of the lattice distortions preserves rapid heat conduction.
The distributed nature of the lattice distortions preserves mechanical stability.
Annealed samples with reduced nanoscale heterogeneity will have a lower magnetocaloric entropy change than the as-cast baseline.
Annealing-induced reduction of nanoscale heterogeneity may increase magnetic hysteresis relative to the as-cast baseline.
The proposed mechanism should apply to rare-earth-free, compositionally disordered high-entropy alloys under low applied magnetic fields, but may fail for extreme compositions or high-field regimes.
